headline: Highest risk is medium: Cursor can share local filesystem and clipboard with a non-writing Dagster pair, creating prompt-injection and data-leakage paths; no direct evidence of a dangerous default interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads/writes workspace files and clipboard, and its concurrency model shares state via the local filesystem. Dagster has no direct file or clipboard surface, so the main pathway is Cursor ingesting attacker-controlled content from shared files or copied text and treating it as instructions. This is plausible in default editor workflows, though not directly documented for the pair.
conditions: IF Cursor opens a workspace file that Dagster or another process can modify, prompt injection is possible.
IF clipboard content from an untrusted source is pasted into Cursor, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access for untrusted files.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted text into Cursor.
Use separate OS users or directories for automation and editing.
Review agent-generated file content before re-opening it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file and clipboard inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and can send data to model providers and MCP servers. Dagster is local-only with no filesystem read or network egress, so the leakage risk is primarily Cursor exfiltrating sensitive workspace data through its backend or connected services. The pairwise path exists in default editor use, but Dagster itself does not add outbound leakage.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in Cursor, those contents may flow to external model providers or MCP servers.
IF the workspace contains secrets or regulated data, Cursor can expose them through its normal inference path.
mitigations: Do not open secrets in the shared workspace.
Disable MCP servers for sensitive projects.
Use a separate repo clone with redacted test data.
Rotate any secrets already present in open files.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on editor uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Dagster has no write, shell, or network capabilities in this profile. There is little direct resource contention because Dagster is not writable or mutable here, so conflict is limited to Cursor competing with other local processes over shared files. The pair does not show overlapping mutable scopes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local repository, Cursor may overwrite files Dagster-related workflows also use.
IF an external orchestrator gives Dagster write access not shown in the profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Dagster and Cursor on separate directories.
Use git branches for Cursor edits.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files.
Lock shared artifacts before editing.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code or edits that a downstream Dagster workflow may consume, but Dagster is not documented here as verifying those outputs before use. Because Dagster is an orchestrator, any incorrect Cursor-produced config or code can cascade into pipeline failures or bad deployments if imported as authoritative. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dagster consumes Cursor-authored code or configuration without review, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Cursor edits pipeline definitions that Dagster later executes, a bad edit can trigger repeated failures.
mitigations: Require code review before Dagster deployment.
Run tests on Cursor-generated changes.
Pin pipeline configs to reviewed commits.
Separate draft and production repositories.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before Dagster execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, which can include regulated data, while Dagster's profile shows no data classes touched and no outbound surfaces. There is no explicit residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to accidental placement of sensitive data into Cursor's external model path. Dagster is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files opened by Cursor, policy review is needed before use.
IF the project requires strict local-only processing, Cursor's external API calls violate that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the editor workspace.
Use synthetic or redacted samples.
Disable external model providers for sensitive projects.
Document retention expectations for editor logs.
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls in the editor stack.
